verse: And now I will break off his yoke from you and snap the chains that bind you. (Nah 1:13)
The Lord has redeemed Jacob, and he has freed him from the hand of one more powerful. (Jer 31:11)
Take courage, my children, cry out to the Lord, and he will rescue you from the power and hand of the enemy. (Bar 4:21)
Behold, I have given you authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and upon all the powers of the enemy, and nothing will hurt you. (Luk 10:19)
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. (Rom 16:20)
If the righteous man is a child of God, God will help him and will deliver him from the hand of his enemies. (Wis 2:18)

Whenever the evil spirit from the Lord assailed Saul, David took up his stringed instrument, and he played it with his hand, and Saul was refreshed and uplifted. For the evil spirit withdrew from him. (1 Sam 16:23)
Let my prayer come before you; deliver me according to your Word. (Ps 119:170)

When that day comes, I will break the yoke that is around his neck and remove his chains, and they will no longer be the slaves of strangers. Instead, they will serve me, the Lord their God. (Jer 30:8-9)
Do not be afraid. Neither should you be dismayed by this multitude. For the battle is not yours, but God’s. (2 Chron 20:15)
The Lord has freed me from every evil attack, and he will preserve me for his heavenly kingdom. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen. (2 Tim 4:18)
I will call upon the Lord, who is worthy to be praised, so shall I be saved from my enemies. (Ps 18:3)
The Lord will cause your enemies who rise against you to be defeated before you. They shall come out against you one way and flee before you seven ways. (Deut 28:7)
No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper, and you shall refute every tongue that rises against you in judgment. (Is 54:17)
For though we walk in the flesh, we do not battle according to the flesh. (2 Cor 10:3)
God is faithful. He will strengthen you, and he will protect you from the evil one. (2 Thes 3:3)
I struck them down, so that they were unable to rise; they fell under my feet. For you girded me with strength for the battle; you subdued my enemies under me. (Ps 18:38-39)
Through you we push down our enemies; through your name we tread down those who rise up against us. (Ps 44:5)
The Lord is a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble. (Ps 9:9)
He delivered me, because he delighted in me. (Ps 18:19)

Put on the full armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against the powers, against the world rulers of this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places. (Eph 6:11-12)

Take up the whole armor of God, so that you may be able to withstand on that evil day, and having done all, to stand firm. Stand therefore and gird your loins with the belt of truth and put on the breastplate of righteousness. For your feet put on anything that will make you ready to spread the gospel of peace. Above all, take the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the fiery darts of the evil one. Take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. (Eph 6:13-17)
He has rescued us from the power of darkness, and he has transferred us into the kingdom of the Son whom he loves. (Col 1:13)
They were all so amazed that they began to ask each other, “What is this? A new teaching with authority! For he commands the unclean spirits, and they obey him.” (Mrk 1:27)

Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee before him. As smoke is driven away, so drive them away; as wax melts before the fire, let the wicked perish before the presence of God. (Ps 68:1-2)
A thousand may fall at your side, ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not come near you. You will only look with your eyes and see the punishment of the wicked. (Ps 91:7-8)
Little children, you are from God and have overcome them because the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world. (1 Jn 4:4)
If God is for us, who can be against us? (Rom 8:31)
You should not fear them. For the Lord your God will fight on your behalf. (Deut 3:22)
Your hand shall be lifted up over your adversaries, and all your enemies shall be cut off. (Mic 5:9)
Rise up, O Lord, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee from your presence. (Num 10:35)
You, my enemy, should not rejoice over me because when I have fallen. I will rise up; when I sit in darkness., the Lord is my light. (Mic 7:8)

All who are incensed against you shall be ashamed and confounded; they shall be as nothing. You shall seek them, but shall not find them, even those that contend with you; those who war against you shall be as nothing at all. For I, the Lord your God, who holds your right hand, says to you, “Do not fear, I will help you. (Is 41:11-13)
I will deliver you out of the power of the wicked and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless. (Jer 15:21)

Do not be afraid. Stand firm and see the great wonders of the Lord, which he will do today. For the Egyptians, whom you now see, will never again be seen. The Lord will fight on your behalf, and you have only to remain silent. (Exo 14:13-14)
On the day when I act, you will trample down the wicked, and they will be like ashes under the sole of your feet. (Mal 4:3)
Because you have made the Lord your refuge, the Most High your dwelling place, no evil shall befall you, no plague come near your tent. (Ps 91:9)

The weapons of our warfare are not human weapons, but they have divine powers to destroy strongholds. We destroy false arguments; we pull down every proud obstacle that is raised against the knowledge of God; we take every thought captive and make it obey Christ. (2 Cor 10:4-5)
Submit yourselves to God. Resist the Devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. (Jas 4:7-8)
Be sober and vigilant. For your adversary, the devil, is like a roaring lion, traveling around and seeking those whom he might devour. Resist him by being steadfast in your faith. (1 Pet 5:8-9)

In the synagogue there was a man who had the spirit of an unclean demon, and cried out with a loud voice, Let us alone! What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are - the Holy One of God.” But Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be quiet, and come out of the man!” When the demon had thrown him down in their midst, he came out of him without hurting him. (Luk 4:33-35)
He healed many who were afflicted with various diseases and cast out many demons; but would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew him. (Mrk 1:34)

They brought to him a demoniac who was mute. And when the demon was cast out, the mute person spoke; and the crowds wondered in amazement and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!” (Matt 9:32-33)
When evening came, they brought to Jesus many who were possessed by demons and He cast out the evil spirits with a word and healed all who were sick. (Matt 8:16)
Jesus was driving out a demon that was mute; when the demon had gone out, the man who was mute spoke, and the people were amazed. (Luk 11:14)
He went throughout the whole region of Galilee, preaching the message in their synagogues and casting out demons. (Mrk 1:39)
Jesus called the twelve disciples together and gave them power and authority over all demons and to cure diseases. (Luk 9:1)

Now these signs will accompany those who believe. In my name, they shall cast out demons. They will speak in new languages. They will take up serpents, and, if they drink anything deadly, it will not harm them. They shall lay their hands upon the sick, and they will be made well. (Mrk 16:17-18)
They went out and preached that everyone should repent. They cast out many demons and anointed with oil many who were sick and healed them. (Mrk 6:12-13)
The seventy-two returned with gladness, saying, “Lord, in your name even the demons submit to us.” And he said to them: “I watched Satan fall from heaven like lightning.” (Luk 10:17-18)
